events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Pier rating for this week: 1 (below average) at all four ports.** No pier salmon reports appear in the last four weeks, so this is my estimate, not a report.
- **Go to Grand Haven if you pier fish.** It has the newest report (July 24), but that report is from boats, not the pier.
- **Try green or orange spoons, or glow spoons and plugs.** Those are what anglers used most recently, from boats and in past pier reports.
- **If the pier is slow, the boat bite is better.** Recent boat reports put fish 35-100 ft down in 60-120 ft of water.

## Why
- There are no pier salmon reports this summer, so I'd expect pier fishing to be below average everywhere, since I have nothing better to go on.
- Surface water is warm (68-73 F on the buoys), above the 52-58 F range that Chinook and coho prefer (NY DEC guidance), so I'd expect the fish to stay offshore and deeper.
- Past pier reports in warm August weeks were mostly slow or "a few fish," which is why I'd rate this week a 1 rather than higher.

## Evidence
**Recent reports (newest is 6 days old, July 24, Grand Haven)**
- Grand Haven, 2024-07-24: boat anglers caught Chinook, with a few coho and steelhead, "35 to 100 down in 60 to 120 feet of water"; green and orange spoons and white flasher flies worked.
- St. Joseph, 2024-07-10: the best boat fishing was "very good" (rated 4) on spoons at 80-90 ft, but that was three weeks ago.
- South Haven, 2024-07-10: boats rated it average (2), best at 75-80 ft and 105-110 ft, with rotators and flies.
- Muskegon, 2024-07-10: boats rated it average (2), 40-100 ft down in 70-120 ft of water; meat rigs and flasher flies.
- St. Joseph, 2024-07-03: boats rated it below average (1); the report says "a few coho salmon and steelhead."

**Past seasons (general history, similar water temperature)**
- Grand Haven, 2023-08-16: "Pier anglers who were casting spoons found the freshwater drum and salmon bite to be slow" (rated 0); glow spoons and plugs worked.
- St. Joseph, 2023-08-09: "Pier fishing was a little on the slow side" (rated 1); coho were caught on nightcrawlers.
- Grand Haven, 2022-08-17: pier anglers caught "a few coho salmon and steelhead" on shrimp or glow spoons (rated 1).

**Conditions now**
- The conditions tool returned only a summary for the week before July 30 (live data was unavailable). Buoy surface water averaged 73 F at St. Joseph, 71 F at South Haven, and 68 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon, each rising 1-2 F that week.
- There was no modeled pierhead water or cold-layer depth, so I can't say whether an upwelling is bringing cold water to the piers now.

## Caveats
- The newest report is 6 days old, and the newest pier-specific salmon data is from 2023. Treat this as a guide.
- The 1 ratings are my inference from boat reports and past pier reports, not from pier reports this year.
- The buoy temperatures are measured; I have no modeled pierhead temperature for this week to check for an upwelling.
- Check the Grand Haven and St. Joseph bulletins for the latest pier reports before you go.
